title: User acceptance testing
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for user acceptance testing: synthetic personas with goals, acceptance criteria a person agrees to before any test, scenario scripts, observed results recorded as they happen, every defect proposed as a finding, and a person's go or no-go kept as a noun.
boundaries: A person agrees to the criteria before testing and signs off after it; an agent never records go or no-go.
Runs use synthetic data and read-only steps; a step that would submit, pay or create an account runs only on a test target a person named.
Failed, blocked and not-run steps stay on the record; a rerun is a new session.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for user acceptance testing with a person's sign-off

value.lets_workers: Write personas and acceptance criteria before testing, have a person agree to the criteria, turn them into scenario scripts, run each script and record what was observed as it happened, propose a finding for every defect, compile the results by a fixed rule, and keep a person's go or no-go as a noun.

flow.when: When a surface, page or change needs acceptance testing.
Before any testing, from the personas and the change.
A person agrees to the exact criteria version; a person's verb.
Once per script and build, by an agent or a person.
When the planned sessions are in; deterministic.
A person records go, no_go or go_with_conditions; a person's verb.

guardrails: Criteria come first and are agreed by a person; a criterion changed after testing starts is a new version, and its runs are repeated.
Record what was observed, as it happened. Never edit a result to match the expected one.
Every failed or blocked step becomes a proposed finding with its evidence.
Only a person signs off. A recommendation from the results is advice, not the decision.
Synthetic test data only. No real names, contact details or case details, ever.
complements: Accessibility findings go through the accessibility audit pack, which cites WCAG success criteria.
Each defect's fix, verification and guard go through the findings to fixes pack.
The launch readiness pack pins a sign-off as evidence before an owner decides on launch.

nouns.title: How acceptance testing runs from personas to a person's sign-off
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: draft-personas writes who the surface is for, as assumptions.
write-acceptance-criteria writes what must be true for each persona, before anyone tests.
agree-criteria: a person agrees to an exact criteria version.
write-scenario-scripts turns the agreed criteria into steps a person or a browser-driving agent can follow.
run-scenario follows one script on one build and records each step's result as it happens.
compile-results derives each criterion's verdict and a recommendation by fixed rules.
sign-off: a person records go, no_go or go_with_conditions, with reasons.
rules: Testing starts only from an agreed criteria version, pinned by digest.
A run on a different build or criteria version than its script ends blocked instead of guessing.
Observed results are recorded in plain words; expected results are never copied into them.
A failed, blocked or not-run step stays on the record; a rerun is a new session.
A no-go is a useful result, not a failure of the testing.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

roles.accountable_person: Agrees to the criteria and signs off. Usually the person who owns the outcome, such as a program manager.
roles.runner: An agent or a person who follows a script. A runner with assistive technology is a person unless an agent's tool truly is that technology.
roles.compiler: A deterministic worker that derives verdicts; it does not judge.

sources: Acceptance criteria in given, when and then form follow common behavior-driven practice; the wording here is original.

nouns.title: How to write a persona for acceptance testing
nouns.category_reason: A reusable method for writing personas; the personas themselves are seed hypotheses.

a_persona_holds: One primary goal, in the persona's words
The context they work in and any time pressure
Device, screen width, input modes and any assistive technology
How much they know about the domain
What success looks like to them
What they must never be asked to do, such as share a client's details
rules: Write goals and situations, not demographics or stereotypes.
Include at least one persona who uses only a keyboard or a screen reader, and one on a small screen, unless the brief says why not.
Personas are assumptions. Each says what evidence would confirm or contradict it, and later evidence can replace it.
Synthetic only: a role label, never a real person's name, story, photo or contact details.
good_label_examples: Volunteer coordinator on a phone between shifts
Retired volunteer using a screen reader at home

nouns.title: How to write acceptance criteria that can be checked
nouns.category_reason: A reusable method for writing testable criteria.

value.form: Given a starting state, when the persona does one thing, then something a person or a deterministic check can observe happens.
rules: One behavior per criterion, with a then that names what is seen, not how it is built.
Priority is must, should or could. Every persona gets at least one must criterion.
Accessibility criteria cite their WCAG 2.2 success criteria from the accessibility audit checklist.
A time-on-task criterion states its threshold and how the time is measured, such as from the first page load to the moment the field is focused.
Content criteria say who must understand the wording, such as a volunteer with no technical background.
Error criteria say what the persona sees after a mistake and how they recover.

nouns.title: Synthetic test data for acceptance testing
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule for which data a test may use.

use: Names that are role labels or plainly invented, such as Test Volunteer A.
Email addresses only at reserved example domains (example.com, example.org, example.net), and only on a test target.
Phone numbers only from reserved fictional ranges, and only on a test target.
never: Real people's names, stories, contact details, case notes or photos.
Anything pasted from a real inbox, case file or spreadsheet.
Credentials of any kind; a step that needs one is blocked until a person provides access outside the record.
value.on_live_targets: On a live public target, a step that would submit, pay or create an account is recorded as not_run unless a person named a test target for it.

nouns.title: How a failed step becomes a finding
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call mapping from an observed failure to a finding's kind, severity and evidence.

finding_kind.error: The surface does something other than its agreed criterion says, such as a button that does nothing.
finding_kind.design_flaw: It works as built, but the persona cannot finish, is misled or needs help to go on.
finding_kind.annoyance: The persona's own frustration, quoted exactly; record who said it and when.
finding_kind.issue: The environment or process got in the way, such as a missing test target or a build that changed mid-session.

provisional_severity.P0: The run exposed personal data or a credential; stop and route it to the security review pack.
provisional_severity.P1: A must criterion fails for a persona with no workaround they could find.
provisional_severity.P2: A must criterion needs a workaround, or a should criterion fails.
provisional_severity.P3: Cosmetic, or a could criterion fails.

evidence: The script and step number, the build and the criteria version
A screenshot digest and the region that shows the problem
The time and what was observed, in plain words
For an annoyance, the person's exact words

nouns.title: How criterion verdicts and the recommendation are derived
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic derivation: the same sessions always give the same verdicts.

criterion.met: Every step that checks it passed, in the latest included session for each persona it names.
criterion.not_met: At least one such step failed.
criterion.not_tested: No step failed, but at least one was blocked or not run, or a named persona has no included session.

value.included_sessions: Only sessions run on the agreed criteria version; others are listed as excluded with the reason.

recommendation.recommend_no_go: Any must criterion is not_met, or any P0 or P1 finding linked to the sessions is open.
recommendation.incomplete: No must criterion is not_met and nothing blocking is open, but at least one must criterion is not_tested.
recommendation.recommend_go: Every must criterion is met and no P0 or P1 finding is open.

value.rule: The recommendation is advice for the person who signs off; it never decides.

nouns.title: Record checks for sign-offs, with synthetic golden sign-offs
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic checks with synthetic known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes them.

value.purpose: Checks every sign-off must pass before anyone relies on its decision. The three synthetic good sign-offs (a no-go, a conditional go and a clean go) pass all of them; each synthetic bad sign-off fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: The decision is go, no_go or go_with_conditions.
The sign-off names the signer's role.
An agent never signs off, under any role name.
The sign-off is dated in UTC.
The signer says why, in their own words.
The decision names the exact results summary it read.
The decision names the exact agreed criteria.
A go with an unmet must criterion or an open P0 or P1 finding lists each accepted risk.
Every accepted risk says why and who owns it.
A conditional go lists its conditions.
Every condition has an owner and a date.
A no-go says what happens next.
A sign-off holds no email addresses or phone numbers.

verbs.title: Draft personas
verbs.summary: Write two to five synthetic personas for the surface or change under test: each with one goal, context, device, access needs and what success means.
verbs.outcome: Persona nouns, each an assumption with the evidence that would test it.

slots.name: audience_brief
slots.description: Pin of a brief naming the surface, its intended users and what they come to do.

steps: Read the brief and write two to five personas with the fields the persona guide names.
Include at least one persona who uses only a keyboard or a screen reader and one on a small screen, unless the brief says why not.
Keep every persona synthetic: a role label, never a real person's name, story or contact details.
Say for each persona what evidence would confirm or contradict it.

acceptance.check: Every persona validates against template.persona's schema.
Every persona has a goal and success_looks_like.
At least one persona has keyboard_only, switch or voice input or names assistive technology, and one has a screen width under 480 pixels, or the output says why not.
No persona holds an email address or phone number.
The personas differ in ways that change what the surface must do.

verbs.title: Write acceptance criteria
verbs.summary: Write the acceptance criteria for the change before any testing: given, when and then, a priority, the personas each serves and WCAG citations for accessibility criteria.
verbs.outcome: An acceptance criteria noun ready for a person to agree to.

slots.name: change
slots.description: Pin of the brief or change description for what is under test.

steps: Write each criterion as given, when and then, with a then that a person or a deterministic check can observe.
Give each criterion a priority of must, should or could and the personas it serves; every persona gets at least one must criterion.
Add accessibility criteria for the paths that matter and cite their success criteria from the pinned checklist.
State a threshold and how time is measured for every time-on-task criterion.
Leave out how the thing is built.

acceptance.check: The criteria validate against template.acceptance-criteria's schema.
Criterion ids are unique.
Every pinned persona appears in at least one must criterion.
Every accessibility criterion cites at least one WCAG success criterion from the checklist.
Each then can be observed without knowing how the thing is built.

verbs.title: Agree to the acceptance criteria
verbs.summary: The accountable person reads every criterion and agrees to an exact version, changes it or refuses it. This template performs nothing itself.
verbs.outcome: A criteria agreement that pins the version testing will use.

slots.name: acceptance_criteria
slots.description: Pin of the criteria to agree to.

steps: Read every criterion; agree to it, change it or remove it, and say why for each change.
Record the exact version you agreed to; testing starts from that version only.
A criterion changed after testing starts gets a new version, and every run that checked it runs again.

acceptance.check: The agreement validates against template.criteria-agreement's schema.
criteria_ref names one exact version with its value SHA-256.
signer_is_person is true and agreed_by_role is filled.

verbs.title: Write scenario scripts
verbs.summary: Turn the agreed criteria into scenario scripts: one per persona and task, with numbered steps, the observation expected at each and the criteria each step checks.
verbs.outcome: Scenario script nouns that cover every must criterion.

slots.name: acceptance_criteria
slots.description: Pin of the agreed criteria version.

target.description: The address of the build under test. The default is a placeholder that never resolves; replace it.

build.description: The exact build, version or commit under test.

steps: Write one script per persona and task: preconditions, then numbered steps, each an action and the expected observation, naming the criteria it checks.
Cover every must criterion with at least one step, and note where a keyboard-only or screen-reader persona acts differently.
Use only synthetic data from the test-data rules.
Set needs_test_target on every step that would submit, pay or create an account, so a run without a named test target records it as not run.

acceptance.check: Every script validates against template.scenario-script's schema.
Every must criterion of the agreed version is checked by at least one step.
Every step has an expected observation.
Every script's criteria_ref equals the agreement's criteria_ref.
A person new to the surface could follow each script without help.

verbs.title: Run one scenario script
verbs.summary: Follow one scenario script on the named build as its persona would, and record each step's result as it happens with evidence for every failure.
verbs.outcome: A session record of observed results, with a finding proposed for every failed or blocked step.

slots.name: scenario_script
slots.description: Pin of the script to follow.

slots.name: criteria_agreement
slots.description: Pin of the agreement naming the criteria version.

test_target_named.description: True only when a person named a test target for steps marked needs_test_target.

steps: Confirm the build and the agreed criteria version match the script before the first step; if either differs, end blocked.
Follow the steps in order and record each result as it happens: pass, fail, blocked or not_run, with the time.
Write what was observed in plain words, never the expected text; attach a screenshot digest and region for every fail.
Record a step marked needs_test_target as not_run unless test_target_named is true; never type real personal data or paste anything from outside the test-data rules.
Propose findings-to-fixes.record-finding for every failed or blocked step with its evidence, and never fix anything during the run.

acceptance.check: The session record validates against template.session-record's schema.
There is one result for every step of the script, in order.
Every fail has at least one evidence item with a SHA-256.
Every blocked or not_run result has a reason.
failed and not_run equal the number of such results.
The output proposes one record-finding verb for each failed or blocked step.

network: Read-only requests to the target the script names. A step marked needs_test_target runs only against a test target a person named; otherwise it is recorded as not_run.

verbs.title: Compile the results
verbs.summary: Derive each criterion's verdict from the included sessions by the verdict rules, link failures to findings and derive a recommendation for the person who signs off.
verbs.outcome: A results summary with verdicts, linked findings and a recommendation that is advice only.

slots.name: findings
slots.description: Pins of findings recorded for failed steps, if any.

steps: Include only sessions run on the agreed criteria version, and list the others under excluded with the reason.
Derive each criterion's verdict by the verdict rules: met, not_met or not_tested.
Link every not_met criterion to its findings, and list failed steps that have no finding yet under unlinked_failures.
Derive the recommendation by the rules and say why; it is advice, not the decision.

acceptance.check: The summary validates against template.results-summary's schema.
Recomputing the verdicts from the pinned sessions by the rules gives the same verdicts.
Every failed step appears under a criterion's findings or in unlinked_failures.
Recomputing the recommendation gives the same value.

verbs.title: Sign off with go or no-go
verbs.summary: The accountable person reads the results summary and records go, no_go or go_with_conditions with reasons. This template performs nothing itself; releasing stays a separate act.
verbs.outcome: A sign-off noun that passes the sign-off checks.
steps: Read the results summary and the open findings it links.
Record go, no_go or go_with_conditions, with your reasons in your own words.
For a go with any unmet must criterion or open P0 or P1 finding, list each one under accepted_risks with why it is acceptable and who owns it.
Give every condition an owner and a date.
Signing off records a decision only; releasing is a separate act with its own record.

acceptance.check: The sign-off validates against template.sign-off's schema.
The sign-off passes every pinned sign-off check.
unmet_must and open_blocking_findings equal the summary's lists.
